description.narrative:
Ethiopia is undergoing ambitious political, economic, administrative and legislative reforms and aspires to become a low middle-income country by 2025. Being the second most populous country in Africa, Ethiopia is in the early stages of a demographic transition with falling death rates and high birth rates, leading to rapid population growth. The population is currently estimated at 112 000 000 and is expected to double by 2050 if same rates continue.
The proposed intervention by UNFPA, their 9th country programme (CP) builds on the previous CP 2017-2020 which Sweden also supported and it aims to end the unmet need for family planning in Ethiopia. During 2020, Sweden provided additional funds of 17 400 000 SEK to UNFPA for their Covid-19 response strategy. Out of these, ca 5 500 000 SEK is expected to spill over to the new country programme.
The intervention encompasses access to modern and comprehensive sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services, end avoidable maternal deaths and end gender-based violence, enable demographic transition for attaining sustainable development, social cohesion, peace and security. The CP also links to relevant national priorities and is centered around four outcome areas:
1 - Sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) 2 - Adolescents and youth 3 - Gender equality and women’s empowerment 4 - Population dynamics
The intervention is expected to result in: 1 - Increased number of women whose demand is satisfied with a modern method of contraception 2 - Decreased mortality rate by increased skilled birth attendance 3 - Increased number of adolescence and youth who have utilized integrated SRH services 4 - Decreased prevalence of physical, sexual and psychological violence against women and girls 5 - Improved policy environment for population dynamics
Combined they are expected to contribute to the prevention of 3.8 million unwanted pregnancies among women aged 15-49 years by 2025 which will enable an accelerated demographic transition in Ethiopia and the empowerment of the country's women, adolescents and youth to exercise their rights.

Etiopien genomgår ambitiösa politiska, ekonomiska, administrativa och lagstiftningsreformer och strävar efter att bli ett medelinkomstland till 2025. Som det näst folkrikaste landet i Afrika befinner sig Etiopien i de tidiga stadierna av en demografisk övergång med fallande dödstal och höga födelsetal, vilket leder till snabb befolkningstillväxt. Befolkningen beräknas för närvarande till ca 112 000 000 och förväntas fördubblas år 2050 om samma utveckling fortsätter.
Den föreslagna insatsen från UNFPA, deras nionde landprogram (CP) bygger på deras tidigare landprogram 2017-2020 som Sverige gav stöd till och syftar till att möta det ouppfyllda behovet av familjeplanering i Etiopien. Under 2020 gav Sverige ytterligare medel till UNFPA för att bidra till deras Covid-19 responsstrategi om 17 400 000 SEK. Utav dessa förväntas ca 5 500 000 SEK spilla över till det nya landprogrammet.
Stödet omfattar tillgång till moderna och omfattande sexuella och reproduktiva hälsotjänster (SRH), undvika mödradöd och avsluta könsbaserat våld, möjliggöra demografisk övergång för att uppnå hållbar utveckling, social sammanhållning, fred och säkerhet. Landprogramet länkar också till relevanta nationella prioriteringar och är centrerad kring fyra resultatområden:
1 - Sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR) 2 - Ungdomars rättigheter och deltagande 3 - Jämställdhet och kvinnors egenmakt 4 - Befolkningsdynamik
Insatsen förväntas leda till: 1 - Ökat antal kvinnor vars efterfrågan uppfylls med en moderna SRH tjänster 2 - Minskad mödradödlighet med förbättrad tillgång på kvalificerade födelseskötare 3 - Ökat antal unga som har använt integrerade SRH-tjänster 4 - Minskad förekomst av fysiskt, sexuellt och psykiskt våld mot kvinnor och flickor 5 - Förbättrad policymiljö för befolkningsdynamik
Kombinerat förväntas de bidra till att förebygga 3,8 miljoner oönskade graviditeter bland kvinnor i åldrarna 15-49 år fram till 2025 vilket möjliggör en snabbare demografisk övergång i Etiopien och stärkta rättighter och egenmakt för landets kvinnor, flickor och ungdomar.

In pursuit of contributing to the fulfillment of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, UNFPA Ethiopia is committed to achieve the following outcomes envisioned in the UNFPA Strategic Plan: By 2025, the reduction in the unmet need for family planning has accelerated. By 2025, the reduction of preventable maternal deaths has accelerated. By 2025, the reduction in gender-based violence and harmful practices has accelerated.
To achieve these outcomes, the following six outputs has since the revision of of the framework which took place 2023 collectively guided and contributed to their fulfillment:
Quality of care and services: Sexual and reproductive health and rights
Output 1: Effective supply chain strengthened for ensuring availability of sexual and reproductive health commodities at all service delivery points including in humanitarian settings.
Output 2: Comprehensive sexual and reproductive health service provision improved and uptake increased in all settings
Gender and social norms
Output 3: Strengthened capacity of government and key stakeholders on prevention, protection of GBV, and provision of services to survivors of GBV and to eliminate harmful practices in all settings
Population change and data
Output 4: Strengthened data systems and evidence that take into account population changes and other megatrends (including ageing and climate change), in development policies and programmes, especially those related to sexual and reproductive health and reproductive rights.
Humanitarian action
Output 5: National and regional service delivery systems have strengthened capacity to provide lifesaving sexual and reproductive health and gender-based Violence information and services for populations affected by crisis
Adolescents and youth
Output 6: Adolescents and youth, particularly those most vulnerable, are equipped with skills & knowledge to make informed choices about their SRH and rights within an enabling environment that promotes adolescent health and wellbeing.

The below results and achievements was reported in the reporting for the year of 2024:
Sexual and Reproductive Health:
UNFPA supplied contraceptives that offered one year of protection for 4,8 million couples.
With UNFPA support, 317 public health facilities we enhanced to report, review and respond to the maternal deaths surveillance system.
222 public health facilities provided comprehensive SRH services. This in comparison to before 2022, when no (0) facilities provided this.
722 women and girls received obstretric fistula treatment, increasing the cumulative total for the program period from close to 5000 in 2020 to almost 7000 by 2024.
Furthermore, skilled health personnel assisted in almost half a million (470,643) deliveries.
Gender and Social Norms
Close to 50 000 survivors of GBV received comprehensive services in accordance with the national protocol, bringing the cumulative numbers of survivors reached to more than 132 000 in 2024 - up from 34,425 in 2020.
GBV prevention and response services reached more than 440 000 women and girls, offering benefits through GBV referrals, specialized services, and information regarding GBV prevention, risk mitigation and the prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA).
More than 660 000 young girls (aged 10-19 years) and women received UNFPA-supported prevention and/or protection services and care related to female genital mutilation (FGM).

Population Change and Data
One (1) new mapping-based report was produced in 2024, bringing the cumulative from zero (0) in 2020 to 10 in 2024.
The number of regional web-based intergrated management information systems and knowledge platforms increased from five (5) in 2020 to 12 in 2024, reflecting UNFPA´s commitment to data-driven decision making.
Humanitarian Action
More than 800 000 emergency populated populations were provided with SRH services and 326 service providers were tained on the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) for SRH.
Youth and Adolescents
In 2024, UNFPA reached more than a million (1 000 085) young people through life skills education, which enables them to enhance their health, social and economic assets while also participating meaningfully in decision making and peace building processes at all levels.
Intergrated HIV prevention initiatives reached more than 113 000 of the most vulnerable young people.
The final results for the full program period July 2021-June 2025 will be reported in the Completion Memo for the contribution.
